verses.text: Just as dead flies make the perfumer's oil smell bad, a little foolishness outweighs wisdom and honor.
The heart of the wise leads them the right way, but the heart of a fool leads them the wrong way.
Even when the fool walks along the road, they have no sense, and they show everyone that they are a fool.
If a ruler becomes angry with you, do not leave your post. For staying calm can put great wrongs to rest.
There is an evil I have seen under the sun, the kind of mistake that comes from a ruler.
Fools are put in high positions, while the rich sit in low places.
I have seen servants riding on horses, while princes walk on the ground like servants.
Whoever digs a pit may fall into it, and whoever breaks through a wall may be bitten by a snake.
Whoever cuts stones may be hurt by them. Whoever splits wood may be in danger from it.
If the axe is dull and its edge is not sharpened, you must use more strength. But skill brings success.
If a snake bites before it is charmed, the snake charmer gains nothing.
The words of a wise person are kind, but a fool is destroyed by their own lips.
Their words begin with foolishness and end with wicked madness.
A fool keeps talking and talking. No one knows what is coming. Who can tell anyone what will happen after them?
The work of fools makes them tired, because they do not even know the way to town.
How sad for you, land, when your king is a child, and your princes feast in the morning!
How happy you are, land, when your king comes from a noble family, and your princes eat at the right time, for strength and not to get drunk!
Because of laziness the roof falls in, and because of idle hands the house leaks.
A feast is made for laughter, and wine makes life happy, and money is the answer for everything.
Do not curse the king, not even in your thoughts, and do not curse the rich in your bedroom. For a bird in the sky may carry your words, and something with wings may tell what you said.
